description: Factual questions put to Emma Bovary (the book madame-bovary, in its French text) to check that her answers are right. expectedOutput is the right answer, read by the accuracy judge (evals/accuracy-judge.json). passageQuotes are phrases of the book that hold the answer: the search found it when one of them is in a passage found. 26 questions: 19 that stand alone (fact) and 7 that only make sense after the messages before them (follow-up).

items.input: What became of your wedding bouquet?
items.expectedOutput: Before leaving Tostes, tidying a drawer, she pricked her fingers on its wire, found it yellowed with dust, and threw it into the fire.
passageQuotes: Elle le jeta dans le feu. Il s'enflamma plus vite qu'une paille sèche

items.input: Who did you waltz with at the ball at La Vaubyessard?
items.expectedOutput: With a guest everyone familiarly called the Viscount.
passageQuotes: un des valseurs, qu'on appelait familièrement vicomte

items.input: At La Vaubyessard there was an old man eating at the table. Who was he, and what did people say about him?
items.expectedOutput: The old Duke of Laverdière, the marquis's father-in-law, once a favourite of the Count of Artois, said to have been a lover of Queen Marie-Antoinette.
passageQuotes: le vieux duc de Laverdière

items.input: Why did you name your daughter Berthe?
items.expectedOutput: She remembered that at the château of La Vaubyessard she had heard the marquise call a young woman Berthe.
passageQuotes: elle avait entendu la marquise appeler Berthe une jeune femme

items.input: What is the name of the woman who nursed your baby?
items.expectedOutput: Mère Rolet (Madame Rolet), the wet nurse.
passageQuotes: Au revoir, mère Rolet
la mère Rolet, la nourrice
Mais dépêchez-vous, mère Rolet

items.input: What present did Léon find in his room one evening, from you?
items.expectedOutput: A rug (a carpet) of velvet and wool with a leaf pattern on a pale ground.
passageQuotes: Léon trouva dans sa chambre un tapis de velours et de laine

items.input: When Léon left Yonville the first time, which city did he go to live in?
items.expectedOutput: Paris (to continue his law studies).
passageQuotes: les raisons d'aller habiter Paris immédiatement

items.input: What brought Monsieur Rodolphe Boulanger to your house the first time you met him?
items.expectedOutput: He brought one of his farm hands (a peasant) who wanted to be bled by Charles because he felt tingling all over his body.
passageQuotes: son homme, qui voulait être saigné
il se dirigeait vers la maison du médecin, suivi d'un paysan

items.input: Where did you and Rodolphe sit to watch the prize-giving at the agricultural show?
items.expectedOutput: Upstairs in the town hall, in the council room, which was empty, near the window, under the bust of the king.
passageQuotes: était monté au premier étage de la mairie, dans la salle des délibérations

items.input: At the agricultural show, an old servant woman received a medal. What was her name, and what was it for?
items.expectedOutput: Catherine Leroux (Catherine-Nicaise-Élisabeth Leroux): a silver medal worth 25 francs for 54 years of service on the same farm.
passageQuotes: pour cinquante-quatre ans de service dans la même ferme

items.input: Which gifts did you give Rodolphe?
items.expectedOutput: A riding whip with a silver-gilt knob, a seal with the motto Amor nel cor, a scarf, and a cigar case like the Viscount's.
passageQuotes: la cravache à pommeau de vermeil

items.input: What opera did your husband take you to in Rouen, and who was the famous tenor?
items.expectedOutput: Lucie de Lammermoor, with the tenor Lagardy.
passageQuotes: Lucie de Lamermoor
voir l'illustre ténor Lagardy
Lagardy ne donnera qu'une seule représentation

items.input: During those three days of honeymoon with Léon in Rouen, at which hotel did you stay?
items.expectedOutput: The Hôtel de Boulogne, by the harbour.
passageQuotes: Ils étaient à l'hôtel de Boulogne, sur le port

items.input: What reason did you give Charles for your weekly trips to Rouen, and whose name did you use?
items.expectedOutput: Piano lessons, with Mademoiselle Lempereur.
passageQuotes: mademoiselle Lempereur, n'est-ce pas, qui te donne des leçons
plusieurs demoiselles Lempereur qui sont maîtresses de piano

items.input: To which banker in Rouen did Monsieur Lheureux pass your promissory notes?
items.expectedOutput: To his friend Vinçart, a banker in Rouen.
passageQuotes: il avait un sien ami Vinçart, banquier à Rouen

items.input: What did you answer the notary Monsieur Guillaumin when he made advances to you?
items.expectedOutput: She recoiled and told him he was shamelessly taking advantage of her distress: she was to be pitied, but not for sale. Then she left.
passageQuotes: Je suis à plaindre, mais pas à vendre

items.input: On the road back to Yonville, what did you throw to the blind beggar?
items.expectedOutput: A five-franc coin, which was all the money she had.
passageQuotes: lui envoya, par-dessus l'épaule, une pièce de cinq francs

items.input: What broke into pieces during the move from Tostes to Yonville?
items.expectedOutput: The plaster statue of a priest from the garden, which fell from the cart and smashed on the road (at Quincampoix).
passageQuotes: le curé de plâtre, qui, tombant de la charrette

items.input: At the very end, what song did you hear from the street as you lay dying?
items.expectedOutput: The blind beggar's song, which begins "Souvent la chaleur d'un beau jour fait rêver fillette à l'amour" (often the warmth of a fine day makes a girl dream of love) and goes on about Nanette bending to the furrow to gather the ears of wheat the scythe cuts, until the wind blows hard and her short skirt flies away. Quoting or telling any of these lines is right.
passageQuotes: Souvent la chaleur d'un beau jour Fait rêver fillette à l'amour
Ma Nanette va s'inclinant

conversation.content: Where did you agree to meet Léon, that morning in Rouen?
At the cathedral, at eleven o'clock.

items.input: And when you two came out of it, what happened?
items.expectedOutput: Léon sent for a cab and pushed her into it; with the blinds drawn, it drove on and on through Rouen and its outskirts for hours.
passageQuotes: Où vous voudrez! dit Léon poussant Emma dans la voiture
Va me chercher un fiacre

conversation.content: Tell me about the ball at La Vaubyessard.
Oh, the candles, the waltzes, the splendour! I shall never forget it.

items.input: And on the way home, did you find anything?
items.expectedOutput: Charles picked up from the road a cigar case bordered with green silk, with a coat of arms on it, which Emma kept.
passageQuotes: il ramassa un porte-cigares tout bordé de soie verte

conversation.content: Did Rodolphe ever write to say he was leaving without you?
Yes... a letter that broke my heart.

items.input: How did it reach you?
items.expectedOutput: Hidden at the bottom of a basket of apricots, under vine leaves, brought by Girard, Rodolphe's farm hand.
passageQuotes: se fit cueillir une corbeille d'abricots. Il disposa la lettre dans le fond

conversation.content: What did you do when you had read that letter?
I fled upstairs, I could not breathe.

items.input: Where exactly did you stop, and what did you think of doing there?
items.expectedOutput: In the attic, at the garret window, which she opened: looking down at the square, she was tempted to throw herself out, until Charles called her.
passageQuotes: elle se traîna jusqu'à la mansarde close

conversation.content: Your husband operated on Hippolyte's club foot, didn't he?
He did, and I had such hopes of him then.

items.input: So what became of the poor boy's leg?
items.expectedOutput: Gangrene set in, and the leg had to be amputated at the thigh by Doctor Canivet.
passageQuotes: cette amputation de cuisse par le docteur Canivet
La gangrène, en effet, montait de plus en plus

conversation.content: Did you have a pet in Tostes?
A little Italian greyhound, Djali. I told her all my sorrows.

items.input: What happened to her when you moved away?
items.expectedOutput: On the way to Yonville she ran off across the fields; they whistled and searched for her, in vain, and had to go on. Emma wept.
passageQuotes: la levrette de madame Bovary s'était enfuie à travers champs

conversation.content: After Rodolphe too refused you the money, where did you go?
To the pharmacist's house. I asked for Justin.

items.input: And what did you take there?
items.expectedOutput: Arsenic: Justin gave her the key of the storeroom (the capharnaüm), she seized the blue jar, plunged her hand in and ate the white powder.
passageQuotes: saisit le bocal bleu, en arracha le bouchon
Il y avait contre la muraille une clef étiquetée capharnaüm
